evidence: A 200 nm InGaAs layer was grown by ALE with 3 s MO exposure, 4s H2 purge, 15 s AsH3 exposure, and 2 s H2 purge. For comparison, another InGaAs layer of the same thickness was grown using conventional MOCVD at the same temperature of 500 1C and a V/III ratio of 120. The lattice-matching condition was obtained by tuning the MO source flow rates. AFM indicates a similar surface roughness, with 0.1 nm for ALE InGaAs and 0.17 nm for conventional InGaAs for 5 /C2 5 mm2 scanning area.
